records.source: ADDING A KIND IS REGISTERING A PROVIDER, not editing a switch. A provider is ``() -> Iterable[HelpEntry]``; :func:`register_provider` adds one and :func:`build_index` calls each of them behind its own guard, so a provider that raises costs its own rows and nothing else. What a result DOES when it is opened is registered the same way, in :mod:`spacr.qt.help_search`.
records.context: Adding a kind is registering a provider, not editing a switch. What a result DOES when it is opened is registered the same way, in :mod:`spacr.qt.help_search`.
records.translation: ACRESCENTAR UM TIPO É REGISTRAR UM PROVEDOR, e não editar um switch. records.label: spacr.qt.help_index#11
records.source: IMPORTING THIS COSTS NOTHING; BUILDING THE INDEX COSTS A SECOND. Every registry is imported inside the provider that reads it, so the module itself pulls in neither Qt nor ``spacr.settings``. Building it measured 1.1 s and 13,000 rows on this tree, which is far too much for the GUI thread -- :mod:`spacr.qt.help_search` runs :func:`build_index` on a worker and this module stays testable without a display.
records.context: Importing this costs nothing; building the index costs a second. Building it measured 1.1 s and 13,000 rows on this tree, which is far too much for the main GUI execution path -- :mod:`spacr.qt.help_search` runs :func:`build_index` on a worker and this module stays testable without a display.

records.label: spacr.qt.help_index.HelpEntry#10
records.source: WHY A TEMPLATE AND NOT THE FINISHED STRING. ``subtitle`` and ``description`` are what the search MATCHES on, so they stay English: the query and the haystack have to be in one language, and the index is built once per session while the interface language can change after it. What the user READS is rendered from the template at the moment a row is drawn, by :func:`rendered_subtitle` and :func:`rendered_description` with :func:`spacr.qt.i18n.tr` passed in -- so a language change is picked up by the next keystroke and this module still imports no Qt and no catalog. "API reference" is the subtitle of ten thousand of the rows; a finished English string here is a wholly English result list for every reader who does not work in English.
records.context: Why a template and not the finished string. ``subtitle`` and ``description`` are what the search MATCHES on, so they stay English: the query and the haystack have to be in one language, and the index is built once per session while the interface language can change after it. What the user READS is rendered from the template at the moment a row is drawn, by :func:`rendered_subtitle` and :func:`rendered_description` with :func:`spacr.qt.i18n.tr` passed in -- so a language change is picked up by the next keystroke and this module still imports no Qt and no catalog. "API reference" is the subtitle of ten thousand of the rows; a finished English string here is a wholly English result list for every reader who does not work in English.
records.translation: POR QUE UM MODELO E NÃO A STRING PRONTA. ``subtitle`` e ``description`` são aquilo com que a busca FAZ A CORRESPONDÊNCIA, então permanecem em inglês: a consulta e o texto pesquisado precisam estar em um mesmo idioma, e o índice é construído uma vez por sessão, enquanto o idioma da interface pode mudar depois. O que o usuário LÊ é renderizado a partir do modelo no momento em que uma linha é desenhada, por :func:`rendered_subtitle` e :func:`rendered_description` com :func:`spacr.qt.i18n.tr` passado como argumento -- assim, uma mudança de idioma é percebida na próxima tecla, e este módulo continua sem importar Qt nem catálogo algum. "API reference" é o subtítulo de dez mil das linhas; uma string pronta em inglês aqui seria uma lista de resultados inteiramente em inglês para todo leitor que não trabalha em inglês.
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)
